title: How to set up a quick connection to Exchange Online via PowerShell
replaces: Profile function Connect-EXOnline: Get-Credential + Basic auth New-PSSession to outlook.office365.com/powershell-liveid + Import-PSSession -> Connect-MspExchangeOnline per customer (technician GDAP token, modern auth), Get-OrganizationConfig check, -KeepConnected for one interactive session
notes: Hub article that many others link to for the connection step. Example 3 in the help shows a profile wrapper, so the quick-connect idea survives. For the partner's own tenant, Connect-ExchangeOnline -UserPrincipalName is still the answer.

title: Set Default Sharing Policy for Office 365 Users' Calendars
replaces: Basic auth RPS + foreach Get-Mailbox: Set-MailboxFolderPermission alias:Calendar -User Default LimitedDetails -> report of the Default calendar permission per user mailbox (Get-EXOMailboxFolderPermission), change behind -Apply/ShouldProcess, addressed by PrimarySmtpAddress, localised calendar folder fallback
notes: Uses PrimarySmtpAddress instead of alias (an alias is not always unique, see article 1189). -AccessRights limited to None, AvailabilityOnly, LimitedDetails, Reviewer. The reference table of access rights stays in the article, not the script. Review: a mistyped -Mailbox is now recorded as Failed and the other mailboxes still run.

title: Export a list of mobile devices connected to Office 365
replaces: Basic auth RPS + Get-MobileDevice -Mailbox per mailbox -> one Get-MobileDevice -ResultSize Unlimited per customer matched to mailboxes by distinguished name, plus access state and managed/compliant flags
notes: Help notes that Intune-enrolled devices are better reported from Intune managedDevices. Review: UserDisplayName, a column of the original export, was added back.

title: Managing Outlook Groups via PowerShell
replaces: List of UnifiedGroup cmdlets after Basic auth RPS -> -Action Report (groups, optional members), AddMember (only missing members) and Create (private group) behind -Apply/ShouldProcess
notes: Outlook Groups renamed to Microsoft 365 Groups. Remove-UnifiedGroup is deliberately not scripted (help explains). New-UnifiedGroup and Add-UnifiedGroupLinks need the delegated path, not app-only. Review: New-UnifiedGroup on its own creates public groups, as the original did. -AccessType (Private default, Public) was added so the original behaviour is still available.

title: Secure the devices that access your Office 365 email
replaces: Same as 1165 (near-duplicate blog post)
notes: Near-duplicate of KB 1165, mapped to the same script. Both URLs are in the script .LINK lines.

title: How to secure the devices that access your Office 365 email
replaces: New-MobileDeviceMailboxPolicy + Get-Mailbox | Set-CASMailbox after Basic auth RPS -> report of EAS policies and assignments (Get-MobileDeviceMailboxPolicy, Get-EXOCasMailbox), optional create + assign behind -Apply/ShouldProcess, via Connect-MspExchangeOnline
notes: Shares one script with the near-duplicate blog post 1152. Help states that most Allow* settings are ignored by Outlook mobile and points to Intune app protection plus Conditional Access as the recommended control. Existing policies are never modified.

title: How to export a list of Office 365 users to CSV
replaces: Connect-MsolService and Get-MsolUser filtered on IsLicensed, plus the Sign-In Assistant and Azure AD module downloads
notes: Graph users with assignedLicenses, and subscribedSkus for SKU names. Both dead prerequisite links can go. The Microsoft 365 admin center Export users button is the no-script alternative.

title: The Sharing policy doesn't allow you to grant certain permissions to users on CalendarFolder folder "Calendar"
replaces: No change needed: Exchange cmdlets only (Add-MailboxFolderPermission, Set-Mailbox), no connection method
notes: Still works as published, so no script. The only improvement is a Connect-ExchangeOnline note. set-default-calendar-permission.ps1 now addresses calendars by primary SMTP address, which avoids the non-unique alias problem this article describes.

title: How to fix the Office 365 WINMAIL.DAT attachment issue
replaces: Set-RemoteDomain Default -TNEFEnabled $false after Basic auth RPS -> per-customer report of the Default remote domain TNEF setting, change behind -Apply/ShouldProcess with readback
notes: The dead help.outlook.com link is replaced with Microsoft Learn in the help.

title: Simplify External Contact and Group Management with Powershell
replaces: Downloadable menu script whose connect option used Basic auth RPS, plus advice to add users to Organization Management -> parameter-driven -Action Report / AddContact / RemoveContact / NewGroup behind -Apply/ShouldProcess, run by a technician with Exchange Recipient Administrator through GDAP
notes: Unsafe original advice (Organization Management for a contact and distribution group tool) replaced: help states Recipient Management, or the Exchange Recipient Administrator GDAP role, is enough. The menu items listed in the article were reproduced. Review: the original DistributionGroups.txt was read. Its "remove a contact" option ran Remove-MailContact (deleting the contact), so -DeleteContact was added to -Action RemoveContact to keep that behaviour. Help now says membership changes on groups the technician does not own need -BypassSecurityGroupManagerCheck and Exchange Administrator.

title: Working with archive policies in Office 365 and SkyKick
replaces: Same as 1525 (blog copy, no connection step shown)
notes: Near-duplicate of KB 1525, mapped to the same script. Both URLs are in the script .LINK lines. The post date (2021) is a re-publish of the 2016 article. Review: see 1525 for the retention policy link fix.

title: Working with Archive Policies in Office 365 and SkyKick
replaces: Manual New-RetentionPolicyTag / New-RetentionPolicy / Set-Mailbox -RetentionPolicy / Enable-Mailbox -Archive / Start-ManagedFolderAssistant after Basic auth RPS -> one idempotent script per customer and mailbox list, report-only by default, -Apply with ShouldProcess, reports archive status and size, runs Enable-OrganizationCustomization for dehydrated tenants
notes: SkyKick framing dropped (help talks about any Google Workspace migration). Help mentions archive licensing and Microsoft Purview retention as the newer approach. Shares one script with blog post 1506. Review: an existing policy with the chosen name that does not link the tag now gets the tag added (Set-RetentionPolicy -RetentionPolicyTagLinks @{Add=...}) instead of being reported as in place, and an existing tag with a RetentionAction other than MoveToArchive is flagged.

title: Remove Work or School account option when signing into Microsoft Account
replaces: Get-MsolUser -ReturnDeletedUsers | Remove-MsolUser -RemoveFromRecycleBin -Force (unfiltered purge of every deleted user)
notes: Works-but-outdated article: only the optional PowerShell purge is replaced. The script is report only: it lists soft-deleted users (directory/deletedItems/microsoft.graph.user, Directory.Read.All) with the deletion date, the purge date and days until the 30-day automatic purge, and returns guidance to permanently delete in the Microsoft Entra admin center (Users > Deleted users > Delete permanently) when really required. It no longer permanently deletes through Graph, and User.DeleteRestore.All was removed from the full manifest: an irreversible, rarely needed action does not justify a standing permission in every customer. The unmanaged-tenant admin takeover stays a manual Microsoft Entra admin center step (GDAP cannot reach an unmanaged tenant), and the article's 'create a new Global Administrator' step should become 'use the admin account created by the takeover, with MFA'. The personal address in the prose still needs a manual edit. -UserPrincipalName names are matched exactly against the deleted form (object ID without hyphens plus the original UPN), so a partial name never selects another account, and each name that is not found gets its own NotFound row. Permanently deleting users who held privileged roles can need Privileged Authentication Administrator.

title: How to set a domain email alias for Office 365 users on a specific domain
replaces: Basic auth RPS + Get-Mailbox | Where PrimarySMTPAddress -match 'domain' + Set-Mailbox -EmailAddresses @{add=alias@newdomain} -> exact domain match, accepted-domain check, address conflict check (Get-EXORecipient), -Apply/ShouldProcess
notes: Uses the local part of the primary address by default (-UseAlias keeps the original behaviour). The -match regex is replaced with an exact suffix match so contoso.com no longer matches contoso.com.au. Contoso placeholders replace the GCITS to GCIT rebrand story. Review: the original text match deliberately caught two domains (example.com and example.com.au), so -MatchDomain now takes several domains.

title: How to remove all Office 365 connected accounts in bulk
replaces: No script: obsolete topic
notes: Outlook on the web Connected Accounts (POP/IMAP subscriptions) stopped syncing on 30 October 2018 and the option was removed in November 2018. Nearest modern alternative for leftover subscriptions that block a mailbox move: Get-Subscription -Mailbox <user> -AggregationType All | Remove-Subscription after Connect-MspExchangeOnline. For migrations use Microsoft 365 IMAP migration or a migration tool.

title: Resolving issues when migrating from Telstra syndicated Office 365 to Office 365 via CSP
replaces: No script: obsolete topic
notes: Telstra syndicated Office 365 no longer exists and the BigPond SPF fix was speculative. Nearest modern alternative: Microsoft cross-tenant mailbox migration (tenant to tenant) guidance on Microsoft Learn. Recommend unpublish, noindex or redirect.

title: Solving issues when migrating away from Telstra's Office 365 to Office 365 via CSP
replaces: No script: obsolete topic
notes: KB copy of the Telstra syndication article (same content as post 1694). Nearest modern alternative: Microsoft cross-tenant mailbox migration guidance. Recommend retire or an obsolete-topic notice.

title: Cannot modify certain Exchange Online properties on Telstra Syndicated Office 365 tenants
replaces: No script: obsolete topic (Telstra framing)
notes: The Enable-OrganizationCustomization error still happens in any dehydrated tenant. Nearest modern alternative: scripts/exchange/enable-mailbox-archive-policy.ps1 detects IsDehydrated and runs Enable-OrganizationCustomization under -Apply before it creates retention tags. Could be retitled as a generic Enable-OrganizationCustomization fix.

title: The proxy address is already being used by the proxy address of another mailbox
replaces: Set-MsolUserPrincipalName, Set-MsolDomain -IsDefault, Exchange basic-auth remote PowerShell, and Set-Mailbox -EmailAddresses SMTP:... (overwrote every alias)
notes: Reports which recipients hold the address (Get-EXORecipient). With -RemoveFrom and -Apply: optional UPN change through Graph, a new primary added with @{Add='SMTP:...'} when needed, then only the conflicting address removed with @{Remove='smtp:...'} and read back. -DefaultDomain uses Graph PATCH /domains/{id} isDefault (the only part that needs the missing permission). The Exchange session is closed per customer.

title: Managing users in Office 365 delegated tenants via PowerShell
replaces: Get-MsolPartnerContract (DAP) to find a tenant ID, Get-MsolUser -TenantId, and a profile function storing the tenant in a global variable
notes: -CustomerName searches customers with Get-MspCustomer and lists their users through Graph. The unsafe part of the original (unblocking a shared unlicensed customer admin and resetting its password to a fixed value to reach Exchange) is removed, not replicated: technicians connect to Exchange Online as themselves with Connect-MspExchangeOnline and an Exchange GDAP role. Review fix: a warning now says when more than one customer matches -CustomerName (the original refused to pick one).

title: Export a list of unused Office 365 licenses in your delegated administration tenants
replaces: Connect-MSOLService -Credential (no MFA), Get-MsolPartnerContract -All and Get-MsolAccountSku -TenantId
notes: Graph subscribedSkus per customer, UnusedUnits = prepaidUnits.enabled - consumedUnits, with warning and suspended units. -OnlyUnused, and -ExcludeSkuPartNumber for free SKUs. Partner Center or distributor billing reports remain the source for what is billed. Review fix: DefaultDomain column restored (the original's PrimaryDomain).

title: How to install the Azure Active Directory PowerShell Module
replaces: Install-Module MSOnline and Connect-MsolService (MSOnline retired 30 May 2025, mislabelled as the Azure AD PowerShell module)
notes: Hub article. No per-customer module or session is needed any more: install and configure MspGdap once (README, docs/03) and this script checks Graph (and optionally Exchange Online) access to each customer through GDAP. The help also covers installing Microsoft Graph PowerShell for single-tenant work with Connect-MspGraph. Keep the article URL so inbound links survive.

title: Enabling the Unified Audit Log on all delegated Office 365 tenants via PowerShell
replaces: Get-MsolPartnerContract (DAP), temporary Global Administrator accounts with a shared password (New-MsolUser, Add-MsolRoleMember 'Company Administrator', Remove-MsolUser) and basic authentication remote PowerShell (Invoke-Command to ps.outlook.com ?DelegatedOrg= and New-PSSession as the temporary admin)
notes: Unsafe original not replicated. The technician's own GDAP Exchange Administrator role runs Get-AdminAuditLogConfig, then with -Apply Enable-OrganizationCustomization (only when dehydrated) and Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true, with readback. No accounts are created. -LegacyAdminPrefix reports (never deletes) leftover temporary admins from the retired script, because a prefix match can hit a real user. Graph read for that option needs User.Read.All, satisfied by User.ReadWrite.All in both manifests.

title: Enabling the Unified Audit Log on all delegated Office 365 tenants via PowerShell
replaces: Same method as KB 1922: MSOnline and DAP, temporary Global Administrator accounts with a shared hard-coded password, basic authentication remote PowerShell
notes: Blog post (type posts) duplicating KB 1922. Shares the same script rather than a second copy. Its .LINK lines list both URLs. The single-tenant 'check and enable' steps map to running the script with -TenantId for one customer. LITEPACK and Telstra notes are obsolete and have no script equivalent.

title: Set Office 365 Password Expiration Policy for all delegated customer tenants
replaces: Connect-MsolService -Credential with a named admin, Get-MsolPartnerContract (DAP), Set-MsolPasswordPolicy -ValidityPeriod 2147483647 and Set-MsolUser -PasswordNeverExpires on every user
notes: Reports each verified domain's passwordValidityPeriodInDays and, with -Apply, sets 2147483647 per domain through Graph PATCH /domains/{id} with readback. Federated domains are skipped. The per-user bulk change is dropped (not needed once the domain policy is set). Synced users follow the on-premises policy. Replaces the original single-tenant snippet, which was missing a closing brace. Review fix: -IncludeUsers restores the original per-user report (PasswordNeverExpires from passwordPolicies, last password change, synced or cloud) as report-only rows. It needs User.Read.All, which the manifest covers.

title: Get a list of every customers' Office 365 administrators via PowerShell and delegated administration
replaces: Connect-MSOLService -Credential (no MFA), Get-MsolPartnerContract -All, Get-MsolRoleMember 'Company Administrator' and Set-MsolUser -BlockCredential from a CSV
notes: Reads active Global Administrator assignments (roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments with $expand=principal), including groups and service principals, with licence state and last sign-in where Entra ID P1 allows. -BlockFromCsv takes the reviewed CSV, re-checks each account and never leaves fewer than -MinimumEnabledAdmins enabled Global Administrator users, then blocks with -Apply (ShouldProcess, readback). PIM-eligible assignments are not included. Replaces the original's wrong 'is an unlicensed Company Admin' message in the all-admins version. Review fix: -RoleName reports any directory role by display name, as the original's $RoleName did. Blocking stays limited to Global Administrators.

title: Connect an Azure Function to Office 365
replaces: Azure Functions v1 timer function, MSOnline (Connect-MsolService -Credential, Get-MsolPartnerContract, Set-MsolPasswordPolicy) under DAP, AES-encrypted stored password, modules uploaded by FTP
notes: Same content as blog post 2063, so both map to one script. Function: scripts/automation/functions/SetPasswordNeverExpires (Functions v4, managed identity and Key Vault, report only unless MSPGDAP_APPLY_CHANGES=true). Graph PATCH /domains/{id} passwordValidityPeriodInDays=2147483647. GDAP: Domain Name Administrator (write), Global Reader (report). Review: a domain that can't be updated is now recorded and the rest continue (the original carried on too), and the notification window is reported. Listing domains also works with Directory.ReadWrite.All in practice, but Learn lists only Domain.ReadWrite.All for the update.

title: Connect an Azure Function to Microsoft 365
replaces: Azure Functions v1 timer function, MSOnline (Connect-MsolService -Credential, Get-MsolPartnerContract, Set-MsolPasswordPolicy) under DAP, AES-encrypted stored password, modules uploaded by FTP
notes: Blog duplicate of KB 2019, same script and function (SetPasswordNeverExpires). The claim that Azure Functions cannot use Key Vault is outdated: functions/profile.ps1 reads the certificate and refresh token through managed identity. Review: see 2019 (per-domain error handling, notification window column).

title: Add your domain name to trusted senders for all delegated Office 365 users
replaces: Connect-MsolService -Credential, Get-MsolPartnerContract, Get-MsolDomain (DAP), Invoke-Command -Authentication Basic to ps.outlook.com ?DelegatedOrg=, Set-ExecutionPolicy Unrestricted
notes: -TrustedSender is a parameter (no hard-coded support address). Report by default (Get-MailboxJunkEmailConfiguration), -Apply adds only missing entries with Set-MailboxJunkEmailConfiguration -TrustedSendersAndDomains @{Add=...} and reads back. Help points to SPF, DKIM and DMARC as the better fix. Execution policy advice dropped.

title: Get email alerts about unused Office 365 licenses with Azure Functions, Azure Storage and Microsoft Flow
replaces: Azure Functions v1 with MSOnline Get-MsolAccountSku, AES-encrypted stored password, Azure Table and Queue storage with the account key, Microsoft Flow
notes: Graph GET /subscribedSkus. Function: scripts/automation/functions/UnusedLicenceAlert writes one queue message per SKU with unused units through an identity-based Storage connection (no account key) for Power Automate to email. Free and viral SKUs excluded by default. GDAP: Global Reader. Review: rows now carry a Message text like the original queue message.

title: Retrieve Office 365 user details with Azure Functions, Microsoft Flow and SharePoint Online
replaces: Azure Functions v1 with MSOnline Get-MsolUser, AES-encrypted stored password, basic-auth Exchange DelegatedOrg remote PowerShell, Microsoft Flow HTTP trigger into a SharePoint list
notes: Graph GET /users plus subscribedSkus for licence names, optional userRegistrationDetails and signInActivity (Entra ID P1 or P2). Flat rows suit Power Automate or a PSA. Function: scripts/automation/functions/UserDetailsReport writes JSON to blob storage. The series design that created Exchange admin accounts is replaced by enable-exchange-app-access.ps1. GDAP: Global Reader, Reports Reader for MFA and sign-in data. Review: restored mailbox type (RecipientTypeDetails via Get-EXOMailbox, -IncludeMailboxType) and last password change, both in the original.

title: Create Exchange Administrators in all customer Office 365 tenants using Azure Functions and Delegated Administration
replaces: Three Azure Functions v1 functions that used MSOnline (New-MsolUser, Add-MsolRoleMember Exchange Service Administrator, Set-MsolUser -BlockCredential) to create a standing Exchange admin with a shared password in every customer, unblocked over HTTP
notes: UNSAFE original NOT replicated. Safe equivalent: Test-MspExchangeAppAccess and Enable-MspExchangeAppAccess give the separate automation app Exchange.ManageAsApp and a directory role (no user, no password), and -LegacyAccountUpnPrefix finds and optionally blocks the standing accounts older scripts created. No function, because enabling needs Privileged Role Administrator just in time. GDAP: Cloud Application Administrator plus Privileged Role Administrator (just in time), Privileged Authentication Administrator to block admin accounts.

title: Get Office 365 users with a specific license type via Powershell
replaces: Get-MsolAccountSku and Get-MsolUser filtered on Licenses.AccountSkuId, written with Out-File
notes: -ListSkus replaces Get-MsolAccountSku. Users are filtered server side with assignedLicenses/any(x:x/skuId eq ...). -OutputPath writes a real CSV (the original's Out-File produced a text table with a .csv name). Review fix: -SkuPartNumber accepts wildcards, matching the original's partial -match filter.

title: Stop SendGrid emails from going to junk for your Office 365 users
replaces: Set-HostedConnectionFilterPolicy -IPAllowList @{add=...} pushed to every customer over Invoke-Command -Authentication Basic (ps.outlook.com ?DelegatedOrg=), Get-MsolPartnerContract (DAP)
notes: Unsafe original (allow-listing a shared ESP IP that the article admits was blacklisted, in every customer) is not replicated. Safe equivalent: audits every connection filter policy's IPAllowList and EnableSafeList, and with -RemoveIpAddress -Apply removes the chosen entries (never adds). Help points to SPF, CNAME-based DKIM and DMARC alignment for the sending service instead.

title: Enable mailbox auditing on all users for all Office 365 customer tenants
replaces: MSOnline and DAP with basic-auth DelegatedOrg remote PowerShell and an Azure Functions v1 job that set a custom mailbox audit action set
notes: Obsolete topic, no script. Mailbox auditing has been on by default since 2019, and the custom action set would narrow auditing (drops MailItemsAccessed and other defaults). Nearest alternative: check Get-OrganizationConfig AuditDisabled and per-mailbox AuditBypassEnabled with Connect-MspExchangeOnline and leave DefaultAuditSet in place, and enable the unified audit log where needed (Set-AdminAuditLogConfig through Connect-MspExchangeOnline, docs/07 Pattern 3).

title: Set up a quick connection to the Office 365 Security & Compliance Center via Powershell
replaces: Profile function Connect-SecurityCompliance: Basic auth New-PSSession to ps.compliance.protection.outlook.com -> Connect-MspSecurityCompliance per customer, Get-RetentionCompliancePolicy check, -KeepConnected
notes: Connect-MspSecurityCompliance was confirmed working with a delegated GDAP token in a live test on 7 October 2026 (Get-RetentionCompliancePolicy), with no separate consent or manifest entry for https://ps.compliance.protection.outlook.com. The help gives the interactive Connect-IPPSSession -DelegatedOrganization fallback. Product name updated to Microsoft Purview.

title: Apply Office 365 Retention Policies to all customers via PowerShell and Delegated Administration
replaces: MSOnline and DAP with basic-auth New-PSSession to ps.compliance.protection.outlook.com ?DelegatedOrg=, plus an Azure Functions v1 version with an AES-encrypted stored password
notes: Uses Connect-MspSecurityCompliance (confirmed in a live test on 7 October 2026). Report only by default, -Apply creates the policy and rule only where the customer has none. Help warns that retain-forever is a records, privacy and licensing decision. Removed the inaccurate claim about eDiscovery and holds being phased out. Function: scripts/automation/functions/RetentionCoverageReport is report only by design. GDAP: Compliance Administrator. Review: restored the original check for SharePoint Online (GET /subscribedSkus service plans), so Exchange-only tenants get Exchange and public folder locations only. Needs Global Reader or License Administrator for that check.

title: Get Office 365 users that are still running Outlook 2007 in all customer tenants
replaces: Search-MailboxAuditLog MailboxLogin events filtered on 'Office/12' over basic authentication remote PowerShell, MSOnline and DAP
notes: No script written. Outlook 2007 has been unable to connect to Exchange Online since 2017, and Microsoft has removed Search-MailboxAuditLog from Exchange Online (mailbox audit data has only been searchable through the unified audit log since 1 March 2025). Nearest modern alternatives: scripts/delegated-reporting/export-sign-in-locations.ps1 -Detailed (Entra sign-in logs include clientAppUsed and the application per sign-in), or the Microsoft Graph Microsoft 365 Apps usage report (GET /reports/getM365AppUserDetail, Reports.Read.All) to find users on old Office clients. The article's MFA allow-list and temporary admin advice should be removed with the article.

title: Transfer all OneDrive files to another user via PowerShell
replaces: Connect-MsolService, Set-SPOUser -IsSiteCollectionAdmin with a Global Admin password, Connect-PnPOnline -Credentials and Copy-PnPFile (retired SharePointPnPPowerShellOnline), and advice to use an admin without MFA
notes: A GDAP technician cannot be made a site collection admin of a user's OneDrive, so a file-by-file copy is not possible through MspGdap. The script uses OneDrive's supported automatic access delegation instead: it sets the successor as the departing user's manager (PUT /users/{id}/manager/$ref, read back) and, with -Apply -RemoveDepartingUser, soft-deletes the user so the manager receives the OneDrive link for the retention period. The 'temporary admin without MFA' advice is removed. Nearest manual alternative: the Microsoft 365 admin center delete user flow ('Give another user access to this user's OneDrive') and Microsoft's 'Simplified file transfer for departing employees'. Review fix: the NextStep switch no longer returns two values when the user is deleted, -WhatIf now previews the deletion as well, and -Apply is refused with -AllCustomers.

title: Transition smoothly between Office 365 CSP partners
replaces: Get-MsolUser and Set-MsolUserLicense -AddLicenses with AccountSkuId, plus a Get-MsolPartnerContract name match (DAP)
notes: Exports each licensed user's SKUs, disabled plans and direct or group assignment, with a ready-made Invoke-MspGraphRequest assignLicense restore command for direct licences. The Telstra to Ingram Micro context is dated, but the topic (CSP or subscription transfer) still applies. Recommends group-based licensing as the better safeguard.

title: Warn users when an external email arrives with the same display name as someone in your organisation
replaces: Basic-auth remote PowerShell (New-PSSession, ?DelegatedOrg=) with MSOnline and DAP, Azure Functions v1 with an AES-encrypted stored password, MFA trusted IP bypass
notes: Reports native controls first (External tag, first contact safety tips, impersonation protection), then keeps the transport rule with regular expression metacharacters escaped in each display name (spaces left as they are) and an 8 KB size guard. MFA trusted-IP advice removed. Optional app-only Exchange via -ExchangeAppId and a certificate. Function: scripts/automation/functions/DisplayNameSpoofRule (report only unless MSPGDAP_APPLY_CHANGES=true). GDAP: Exchange Administrator (write), Global Reader (report).

title: Sync Office 365 users with a MailChimp List
replaces: Get-MsolPartnerContract (DAP), Get-MsolUser -TenantId and a Mailchimp API 3.0 bulk subscribe with a plain-text API key
notes: The unsafe original (bulk-subscribing customers' end users without individual opt-in, likely contrary to the Spam Act 2003, plus an API key in the script) is not replicated. The safe equivalent exports enabled licensed member users with licence segments and ConsentStatus NotRequested, for import as pending contacts with double opt-in. Nothing is written to a marketing platform. Consider retiring the article instead. The downloadable .txt attachments were not inspected. The 'Exchange Online Plan 1 users should upgrade for Teams' advice is outdated. Review fix: DisplayName column added, and blank first or last names fall back to the display name as in the original. The help explains how to handle people who are no longer licensed (the original unsubscribed them).

title: Find and remove unnecessary licenses on shared mailboxes in Office 365 customer tenants
replaces: Get-MsolPartnerContract, Get-MsolUser, Set-MsolUserLicense (MSOnline and DAP), Invoke-Command -Authentication Basic to ?DelegatedOrg= (no MFA support), interactive Read-Host menu
notes: Adds the safety checks the original lacked: mailbox size (Get-EXOMailboxStatistics) against 50 GB, active archive, litigation hold, in-place holds, retention hold, and group-assigned licences. Only mailboxes with none of these are SafeToRemove. -Apply removes directly assigned SKUs through POST /users/{id}/assignLicense with readback, and ConfirmImpact High prompts per mailbox unless -Confirm:$false. ReAddSkuIds replaces the Set-MsolUserLicense re-add commands. Least-privileged Graph permissions (User.Read.All, LicenseAssignment.Read.All, LicenseAssignment.ReadWrite.All) are not in the manifests but User.ReadWrite.All and Directory.ReadWrite.All in partner-app.full.json cover them. Review: readback now checks direct assignments only (licenseAssignmentStates), so a SKU also assigned by a group is not reported as a failed removal. GDAP role note corrected: Exchange Administrator alone cannot read users through Graph, so use Global Reader (or add Directory Readers).

title: Export a list of Office 365 users and their licenses in all customer tenants with delegated administration
replaces: Connect-MsolService, Get-MsolPartnerContract -All and Get-MsolUser -TenantId -All with Licenses.AccountSkuId
notes: One row per licensed user with SKU part numbers, group-assigned SKUs, sign-in state and usage location. Replaces the misnamed $licensedSharedMailboxProperties variable.

title: Automate API calls against the Microsoft Graph using PowerShell and Azure Active Directory applications
replaces: AzureAD and AzureRM app creation in one tenant, Azure AD Graph oauth2PermissionGrants, v1 token endpoint, optional ROPC password grant, removed beta reports/getTenantSecureScores
notes: Same job as 2801 with the partner app instead of a per-tenant app, so both map to one script (works for one tenant or -AllCustomers). Graph GET /security/secureScores and secureScoreControlProfiles (v1.0). KB 4630 is the article-level modern replacement. GDAP: Security Reader. Review: per-category scores (Identity, Data, Device, Apps, Infrastructure) and the all-tenants average restored, as the original exported account, data and device scores.

title: Find and remove unnecessary licenses on shared mailboxes in your own Office 365 tenant
replaces: Connect-MsolService -Credential (no MFA), Set-MsolUserLicense -RemoveLicenses, and Exchange basic-auth Invoke-Command against powershell-liveid?DelegatedOrg=
notes: Get-EXOMailbox -RecipientTypeDetails SharedMailbox plus Graph assignedLicenses. Flags mailboxes that must keep a licence (45 GB or more by default, online archive, litigation hold, other holds) and never removes licences from those or group-assigned licences. -Apply removes direct licences with ShouldProcess and readback, and every row carries a restore command. Replaces the original's undefined $customer.TenantId, the 'l: Press q' menu text and the use of the automatic $input variable. Review fix: mailbox size is read with Get-EXOMailboxStatistics -ExchangeGuid instead of the Entra object ID.

title: Automate creation of Azure AD Applications to access the Microsoft Graph in all customer tenants
replaces: AzureAD and AzureRM app with a client secret created in every DAP customer, Azure AD Graph, v1 token endpoint and ROPC, removed beta getTenantSecureScores, secrets exported to CSV
notes: No per-customer app or secret. Graph v1.0 secureScores per customer through GDAP. Recommend a 301 to KB 4630 as the notes suggest. GDAP: Security Reader. Review: see 2773 (category scores restored).

title: Find all Inbox Rules that forward mail externally from Office 365 with PowerShell
replaces: Basic authentication remote PowerShell (single tenant and ?DelegatedOrg=), Connect-MsolService and Get-MsolPartnerContract (DAP), MFA IP allow-listing
notes: Read only. Covers both original scripts. Adds RedirectTo to ForwardTo and ForwardAsAttachmentTo, and reports the default outbound spam policy AutoForwardingMode, because Automatic now blocks external auto-forwarding. Review: added MailboxDisplayName and RuleDescription columns, which the original exported and the first rewrite dropped.

title: Block Inbox Rules from forwarding mail externally in Office 365 using PowerShell
replaces: Basic-auth remote PowerShell and DelegatedOrg sessions with MSOnline and DAP, Azure Functions v1 with an AES-encrypted stored password, MFA trusted IP bypass
notes: Default method is the outbound spam policy AutoForwardingMode (Microsoft recommended, Automatic means Off). -Method TransportRule recreates the original rule, with the original name-mismatch bug fixed. The original Function processed zero tenants ($customers = @()), fixed. Function: scripts/automation/functions/BlockExternalForwarding (report only unless MSPGDAP_APPLY_CHANGES=true). GDAP: Exchange Administrator or Security Administrator. Review: GDAP note corrected, Security Administrator can change the outbound policy but not mail flow rules.

title: Export a list of customers with more than a certain number of licensed Office 365 users
replaces: AzureAD module Connect-AzureAD -Credential (no MFA), Get-AzureADContract (DAP), Get-AzureADUser and Get-AzureADSubscribedSku per customer
notes: -MinimumLicensedUsers (default 5, matching the original), with -IncludeAll for a MeetsThreshold column. The Licences column shows each SKU with its consumed units.

title: Export a list of locations that Office 365 users are logging in from
replaces: Search-UnifiedAuditLog -Operations UserLoggedIn over basic authentication remote PowerShell (single tenant and ?DelegatedOrg=), Get-MsolPartnerContract, Get-MsolCompanyInformation (DAP), IP geolocation through http://ip-api.com
notes: Uses Microsoft Graph GET /auditLogs/signIns?$filter=createdDateTime ge ... (v1.0, AuditLog.Read.All delegated, Learn lists Global Reader, Reports Reader, Security Reader, Security Administrator, Security Operator), whose records already carry city, state and countryOrRegion, so no customer IP addresses go to a third party. Summary per user, IP and location by default, -Detailed per sign-in. Needs Entra ID P1 or P2 in the customer, otherwise that customer is reported as Failed. The v1.0 list returns interactive sign-ins only, 30-day retention. 'Original Version' scripts are not carried over. Review: Graph v1.0 sign-ins carry no ISP or raw user agent, so a Devices column (deviceDetail operating system and browser) replaces the original UserAgent column. Security Operator and Security Administrator added to the supported GDAP roles per Microsoft Learn.

title: Sync Office 365 tenant info with IT Glue
replaces: MSOnline and DAP (Get-MsolPartnerContract, Get-MsolCompanyInformation, Get-MsolDomain, Get-MsolAccountSku, Get-MsolUser), Azure Functions v1 with an AES-encrypted stored password, IT Glue API key in the script
notes: Graph organization, subscribedSkus and users. IT Glue upsert is optional and needs -Apply, the API key comes from SecretManagement and is only sent to the configured IT Glue host. Matching by -ITGlueOrganizationMapPath or, as in the original, contact email domains. Fixed the $licenseTable leak bug. Function: scripts/automation/functions/TenantInfoSync. GDAP: Global Reader.

title: Monitor Office 365 admin role changes in all customer tenants
replaces: Azure Functions v1 with MSOnline Get-MsolRole and Get-MsolRoleMember, AES-encrypted stored password, AzureRmStorageTable state with the storage key, Microsoft Flow
notes: Uses the Entra directory audit log (GET /auditLogs/directoryAudits, category RoleManagement) so additions AND removals are reported without stored state, plus optional current role assignments. Function: scripts/automation/functions/AdminRoleChangeAlert (daily, 25 hour window, queue output). GDAP: Security Reader or Reports Reader, Global Reader for current assignments. Review: role names of removals now read from oldValue (newValue is an empty JSON string).

title: Resolve Winmail.Dat Attachment Issue for all Office 365 Customer Tenants
replaces: Connect-MsolService -Credential, Get-MsolPartnerContract, Get-MsolDomain (DAP) and New-PSSession -Authentication Basic to outlook.office365.com ?DelegatedOrg=
notes: Report by default (Get-RemoteDomain Default TNEFEnabled), -Apply runs Set-RemoteDomain -Identity Default -TNEFEnabled $false with readback. IP allow-list advice dropped. scripts/exchange/disable-tnef-remote-domain.ps1 (another group) covers the single-tenant article.

title: Give an Office 365 user access to all calendars via PowerShell
replaces: Basic authentication remote PowerShell (single tenant and ?DelegatedOrg=), Get-MsolPartnerContract filtered by company name, MFA IP allow-listing
notes: -AccessRight is now mandatory (no PublishingAuthor default) so the operator chooses the lowest level. Finds the calendar folder by FolderType through Get-EXOMailboxFolderStatistics -Folderscope Calendar, so localised folder names work. Fixes the original's try/catch bug (Add-MailboxFolderPermission -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue never reached Set-): it now chooses Add or Set from the current permission and reads back. Company-name filtering is replaced by -TenantId.

title: Monitor External Mailbox Forwards in all Office 365 Customer tenants
replaces: Azure Functions v1 with MSOnline and DAP, AES-encrypted stored password, basic-auth DelegatedOrg remote PowerShell, Azure Table REST signed with the storage key, HTTP function protected only by a function key that removed forwards
notes: Get-EXOMailbox for ForwardingSmtpAddress and ForwardingAddress, optional inbox rule scan, external test against accepted domains, and the outbound policy AutoForwardingMode for context. Removal only interactively with -Apply and ShouldProcess, never over HTTP. Function: scripts/automation/functions/ExternalForwardingReport (report only, queue output). GDAP: Exchange Administrator (remove), Global Reader (report). Review: -Apply now clears only the forwarding setting that points outside the organisation, and the function keeps a state blob so each forward is queued once (the original only alerted on new forwards).

title: Find external forwarding mailboxes in all Office 365 customer tenants with PowerShell
replaces: Connect-MsolService -Credential, Get-MsolPartnerContract, Get-MsolDomain (DAP), New-PSSession -Authentication Basic to ?DelegatedOrg=, MFA IP allow-listing
notes: Read only. Adds the ForwardingAddress check the original missed (resolved with Get-Recipient to a mail contact's external address) alongside ForwardingSmtpAddress, and reports AutoForwardingMode. Review: added the MailboxDisplayName column, which the original exported.

title: Find external forwarding mailboxes in Office 365 with PowerShell
replaces: Single-tenant Basic auth RPS + Get-Mailbox ForwardingSmtpAddress check to a C:\temp CSV -> per-customer Get-EXOMailbox check of ForwardingSmtpAddress and ForwardingAddress (external contacts), optional Get-InboxRule forward/redirect check, reports the default outbound spam policy AutoForwardingMode, -OutputPath creates the folder
notes: Closes the gaps the inventory noted: ForwardingAddress forwards, inbox-rule forwards and the outbound spam policy default. The multi-tenant sibling article belongs to another family.

title: Increase all Office 365 E3 mailboxes to 100 GB via PowerShell
replaces: Connect-MsolService -Credential and Get-MsolUser licence-name matching (no -All, so only 500 users), Get-MsolPartnerContract (DAP), basic authentication remote PowerShell (single tenant and ?DelegatedOrg=), MFA IP allow-listing
notes: Instead of matching licence names, compares each user mailbox's ProhibitSendReceiveQuota with its own mailbox plan (Get-MailboxPlan), so it works for E3, E5 and Business plans and follows future limit changes. -Apply sets ProhibitSendReceiveQuota, ProhibitSendQuota and IssueWarningQuota to the plan values (in bytes, or Unlimited) with Set-Mailbox and reads back. Topic is largely obsolete since 100 GB is the default, so this is mostly a straggler report.

title: Privileged access management in Office 365
replaces: Single New-ElevatedAccessRequest example -> read-only per-customer report of PAM state (Get-OrganizationConfig ElevatedAccessControl), approval policies (Get-ElevatedAccessApprovalPolicy) and requests (Get-ElevatedAccessRequest)
notes: Raising a request stays a manual step (example in help). The PAM cmdlets are documented in the Microsoft Purview PAM configuration article, not the Exchange cmdlet reference (the inventory found the reference page returns 404), so output properties are read defensively. Licensing wording updated away from the Advanced Compliance SKU. Review: request status is read from RequestStatus, the property the Purview PAM article uses.

title: How to disable POP and IMAP for all Mailboxes in Office 365
replaces: Basic authentication remote PowerShell (single tenant and ?DelegatedOrg=), Get-MsolPartnerContract and Get-MsolDomain (DAP), MFA IP allow-listing
notes: Covers both original scripts (single tenant is -TenantId with one value). Reads Get-CASMailboxPlan and Get-EXOCasMailbox -Filter 'PopEnabled -eq $true -or ImapEnabled -eq $true', -Apply runs Set-CASMailboxPlan and Set-CASMailbox with readback. -ExcludeMailbox leaves known OAuth POP or IMAP integrations alone. Help notes that basic auth for POP and IMAP is already retired. Review: a change that does not read back as off is now reported with Status Failed, matching the other scripts.

title: Get alerts for Elevation of Privilege operations on all Office 365 customer tenants
replaces: New-ActivityAlert -Type ElevationOfPrivilege (activity alerts, replaced by alert policies) over basic authentication Security and Compliance remote PowerShell with ?DelegatedOrg=, Get-MsolPartnerContract (DAP)
notes: Reports the default 'Elevation of Exchange admin privilege' alert policy (present, enabled, recipients) and, with -Apply, creates a single-event custom policy with New-ProtectionAlert -ThreatType Activity -Operation Add-RoleGroupMember -AggregationType None -Category AccessGovernance -NotifyUser. Learn says Exchange admin audit records are logged by cmdlet name, but does not list Add-RoleGroupMember as an operation value explicitly, so test the policy in one customer. Uses Connect-MspSecurityCompliance, which was confirmed working in a live test on 7 October 2026. Security and Compliance PowerShell ignores -WhatIf, so the script gates New-ProtectionAlert with its own ShouldProcess.

title: Check Office 365 accounts against Have I Been Pwned breaches
replaces: Connect-MsolService and Get-MsolUser -All (single tenant), Get-MsolPartnerContract -All with Get-MsolUser -TenantId (DAP), an HIBP key typed into the script, and a TLS 1.2 workaround
notes: Covers both the single-tenant and all-customers scripts (-TenantId or -AllCustomers). Graph users (guests skipped) with proxyAddresses and lastPasswordChangeDateTime, HIBP v3 breachedaccount with truncateResponse=false and the required user-agent header, the key from SecretManagement (Get-Secret), Retry-After handling and a configurable delay. Adds PasswordChangedSinceBreach. The USD 3.50 price in the article is out of date, and HIBP domain search is the cheaper option for large tenants. Review fix: HIBP Description, IsFabricated and IsRetired columns restored, and a clean customer now returns a NoBreachesFound row with the number of addresses checked.

title: Allow Passwordless Authentication for all delegated Office 365 tenants
replaces: AzureADPreview Connect-AzureAD -Credential (no MFA), Get-AzureADContract (DAP) and New-AzureADPolicy -Type AuthenticatorAppSignInPolicy, plus MFA trusted-IP bypass advice
notes: Uses the Authentication methods policy (GET and PATCH /policies/authenticationMethodsPolicy/authenticationMethodConfigurations/microsoftAuthenticator). Enables Authenticator for all users with authenticationMode any when disabled, or switches existing targets from push to any while keeping their groups, with readback. The MFA trusted-IP bypass is removed. The help points to passkeys in Microsoft Authenticator for phishing-resistant passwordless sign-in. Placed in users-and-licensing because it is a per-tenant sign-in setting. Review fix: isRegistrationRequired is carried over when include targets are rewritten.

title: Enable MFA on all global admins in customers' Office 365 Tenants
replaces: Get-MsolPartnerContract (DAP), Get-MsolRoleMember 'Company Administrator' and Set-MsolUser -StrongAuthenticationRequirements (legacy per-user MFA), plus scripts that removed MFA and blocked admins
notes: Rewritten as 'report admins without MFA and enforce it with Conditional Access': userRegistrationDetails (isAdmin, isMfaRegistered, methods), security defaults state and enabled CA policies that require MFA for admins. -CreateConditionalAccessPolicy -Apply creates Microsoft's 'Require MFA for administrators' policy (14 role template IDs, break-glass exclusions with -ExcludeUserId) in report-only state. Never turns MFA off. userRegistrationDetails skips disabled users. The header image reused from an unrelated article still needs replacing. Review fix: a tenant whose Conditional Access or registration report cannot be read (for example no Entra ID P1) is still reported with the reason in Error, and no policy is created there. The help points to export-global-admins.ps1 -BlockFromCsv for the original's blocking step.

title: Outlook on the web - Conditional Access
replaces: Set-OwaMailboxPolicy -ConditionalAccessPolicy ReadOnly after Basic auth RPS, plus manual Azure AD portal steps -> per-customer report of OWA mailbox policies and Conditional Access policies with app enforced restrictions (Graph v1.0 identity/conditionalAccess/policies), optional Set-OwaMailboxPolicy and creation of a report-only CA policy behind -Apply/ShouldProcess
notes: The CA policy is created in enabledForReportingButNotEnforced state with optional -ExcludeGroupId for emergency access accounts. Naming updated to Microsoft Entra ID P1/P2.

title: Create a SharePoint Application for the Microsoft Graph via PowerShell
replaces: AzureAD and AzureRM app with tenant-wide app-only Sites.Manage.All, 99-year client secret exported to CSV, v1 token endpoint, deleted any app with a matching name
notes: Creates a single-tenant app with Sites.Selected and a certificate (no secret), grants admin consent and write or read on one site via POST /sites/{id}/permissions. Never deletes apps, reports an existing name instead. No -AllCustomers by design. GDAP: Cloud Application Administrator, Privileged Role Administrator (Graph app role), SharePoint Administrator. Review: retries service principal creation while the new app replicates, and returns the app ID if a later step fails.

title: Sync IT Glue organisations with a SharePoint List via PowerShell
replaces: Azure Functions 1.x experimental PowerShell timer function, client credentials token from the v1.0 endpoint (oauth2/token, resource=, client secret), app created with the AzureAD module (Sites.Manage.All application permission), IT Glue key and client secret in script or plain app settings
notes: Partner-tenant script: Graph goes through Invoke-MspGraphRequest -PartnerTenant with the technician's delegated token (or Pattern B in docs/08 for a scheduled Functions 4.x run), and the IT Glue key comes from Get-Secret. Takes -SiteId and -ListName instead of -TenantId or -AllCustomers, documented in the help. Report only by default, -Apply creates and updates items, -RemoveStale deletes, -CreateList creates the list. New -MatchCustomers fills a CustomerTenantId column from Get-MspCustomer by exact name. IT Glue pagination refuses links.next outside the IT Glue host so the key can't leak. Least-privileged Sites.Manage.All (for -CreateList only) is not in the manifest but Sites.FullControl.All in partner-app.full.json covers it. Not in partner-app.minimal.json: Sites.ReadWrite.All.

title: Sync UniFi Sites with IT Glue
replaces: Legacy UniFi controller API with an admin username and password (POST /api/login on :8443, /api/s/{site}/stat/device), client credentials token from the v1.0 endpoint with a client secret, AzureAD-created SharePoint app, IT Glue key, client secret and UniFi password pasted into the script
notes: Reduced scope, stated in the help: syncs device configurations only (create by MAC address, update name and primary IP) from the official UniFi Network integration API (X-API-KEY, /v1/sites and /v1/sites/{id}/devices with offset and limit paging) into IT Glue, using the original SharePoint match register (UnifiSiteName plus ITGlue lookup to the ITGlue Org Register) read with Invoke-MspGraphRequest -PartnerTenant. Matches sites on the integration API's internalReference, which holds the legacy site name. The UniFi Site flexible asset (Wi-Fi, LAN and WAN, port forwards, VPNs, alarms) and the step 3 match-register builder are not rewritten because those endpoints are not in the official API. Recommend IT Glue's native UniFi integration for them. -ConfigurationTypeId and -ConfigurationStatusId are required instead of creating types. The integration API path and fields should be checked against the console version before first use. Graph read needs Sites.Read.All, covered by Sites.ReadWrite.All in partner-app.full.json. Review: existing IT Glue configurations are now only updated with -UpdateExisting, matching the original default ($overwriteExisting = $false). Help now states that manufacturer, model and serial number IDs are not set and that the match-register builder script is not rewritten.

title: Automatically request IT Glue Quick Notes from your team
replaces: Azure Functions 1.x experimental PowerShell timer and HTTP functions ($req, Out-File $res), IT Glue API key pasted into both functions, Microsoft Flow HTTP trigger URL in the script
notes: One script with two modes matching the two original functions: -RequestNotes (random organisations without quick notes, one per technician from a partner-tenant group via Invoke-MspGraphRequest -PartnerTenant or from -Technician, POST to the Power Automate trigger URL read from the vault) and -AppendNote (HTML-encodes the approval comment, then PATCHes organizations/{id} quick-notes). Both report only without -Apply. Help covers hosting on Functions 4.x with PowerShell 7.6, managed identity to Key Vault and Entra authentication on the HTTP trigger. No Microsoft customer tenant is involved, so no -TenantId or -AllCustomers. GroupMember.Read.All (least privilege for -TechnicianGroupId) is not in the manifest but Directory.ReadWrite.All in partner-app.full.json covers it.

title: Sync Microsoft Secure Scores with IT Glue
replaces: AdminAgents (DAP) app from 4514 with hard-coded secret and IT Glue key, v1 token endpoint, Graph contracts and beta Secure Score endpoints, SharePoint list for org matching
notes: Graph v1.0 secureScores and secureScoreControlProfiles, per-category scores and HTML control tables in the same IT Glue traits as the original. IT Glue upsert optional with -Apply, matching by -ITGlueOrganizationMapPath, key from SecretManagement. GDAP: Security Reader. Review: restored the original contact email domain matching when -ITGlueOrganizationMapPath is not given.

title: Create an Azure AD application with access to customer tenants
replaces: AzureAD and AzureRM multi-tenant app with a 99-year secret exported to CSV, service principal added to AdminAgents for access to every DAP customer
notes: AdminAgents pre-consent no longer works under GDAP. Create the app once with New-MspPartnerApp, then this script runs Test-MspPartnerAppConsent and, with -Apply, Grant-MspPartnerAppConsent per customer. GDAP: Cloud Application Administrator in each customer, AdminAgents in the partner tenant for Partner Center. Review: the customer name now comes from the partner tenant, so a customer without consent is reported as WouldGrant instead of failing.

title: Retrieve customers' Office 365 Message Center info via PowerShell and the Office 365 Management API
replaces: AzureAD and AzureRM app added to AdminAgents (DAP), v1 token endpoint for manage.office.com, retired Office 365 Service Communications API
notes: Graph GET /admin/serviceAnnouncement/messages with text, action-required and age filters. The Skype for Business upgrade example is obsolete. GDAP: Message Center Reader or Global Reader. Review: message body (plain text) restored to the output, as the original exported the message text.

title: Running Delegated Admin PowerShell Scripts with MFA enabled accounts
replaces: Advice to add office and Azure Function outbound IPs to legacy per-user MFA trusted IPs so password-only delegated admin scripts keep working
notes: Obsolete topic, no script. The advice contradicts Partner Center mandatory MFA, and Azure Function outbound IPs are shared with other Azure customers. Nearest alternative: GDAP with per-technician refresh tokens registered with MFA (docs/03) and app-only certificates for unattended jobs (docs/08), with Conditional Access named locations for the automation account. Retire or redirect.

title: Sync mailbox usage reports with a SharePoint list
replaces: AzureAD and AzureRM multi-tenant app added to AdminAgents (DAP), client secret exported to CSV and in function code, Graph contracts and v1 token endpoint, Azure Functions v1 timer and HTTP functions
notes: Graph GET /reports/getMailboxUsageDetail (CSV) with percent of the prohibit send and receive quota and a concealed-names flag. Function: scripts/security-and-graph-apps/functions/MailboxUsageReport queues mailboxes over the threshold. The Acknowledge or Ignore HTTP function is not recreated (Power Automate can handle that from the queue). GDAP: Reports Reader. Review: warning and prohibit send quotas and deleted items restored, and -ExcludeUserPrincipalName (MSPGDAP_MAILBOX_USAGE_EXCLUDE in the function) replaces the original Always ignore.

title: Manage Office 365 customers' security alerts with SharePoint, Microsoft Flow and Azure Functions
replaces: AzureAD and AzureRM multi-tenant app added to AdminAgents (DAP), 99-year secret in function code, legacy Graph /security/alerts (retires 15 October 2026), Azure Functions v1 timer and HTTP functions, Microsoft Flow
notes: Graph /security/alerts_v2 list, and resolve plus comment (PATCH alerts_v2/{id}, POST comments) only with -Apply. Function: scripts/security-and-graph-apps/functions/SecurityAlertSync queues open alerts every 30 minutes. The HTTP resolve function is not recreated, resolving stays interactive. GDAP: Security Reader (read), Security Operator (resolve). Review: the function queued every open alert on every 30 minute run. It now keeps a state blob so each alert is queued once.

title: Delete specific emails from Office 365 inboxes in customer tenants via PowerShell
replaces: AdminAgents (DAP) multi-tenant app with tenant-wide application Mail.ReadWrite and a 99-year secret, searching and deleting messages in every mailbox through Graph
notes: Replaced the tenant-wide Mail.ReadWrite app with a Microsoft Purview content search (New-ComplianceSearch) and an optional SoftDelete purge (New-ComplianceSearchAction -Purge) through Connect-MspSecurityCompliance (confirmed in a live test on 7 October 2026). Search reports counts first, purge only with -Apply. No -AllCustomers by design. Threat Explorer is the alternative where Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 exists. GDAP: Compliance Administrator for the search, Search And Purge (Organization Management, Global Administrator just in time) for the purge.

title: Check provisioning status of Shared Computer Activation for Microsoft 365 Business customers
replaces: Get-MsolPartnerContract -All and Get-MsolAccountSku -TenantId reading the Shared_Computer_Activation service plan provisioning status of SPB
notes: Obsolete topic, no script written. The 2019 rollout of shared computer activation to Microsoft 365 Business Premium finished long ago, so its provisioning status no longer needs checking. Nearest modern alternative: shared computer activation is included in Business Premium and is turned on per device (Office Deployment Tool SharedComputerLicensing=1, Group Policy or Intune). If a check is still wanted, scripts/delegated-reporting/export-unused-licences.ps1 lists each customer's SKUs, and Graph subscribedSkus servicePlans shows each plan's provisioningStatus. Recommend redirecting or unpublishing the article.

title: Sync Azure Active Directory Risk Events with a SharePoint list for all customer tenants
replaces: AzureAD and AzureRM app added to AdminAgents (DAP), client secret in the script, removed beta identityRiskEvents API, SharePoint list with Alert me
notes: Graph GET /identityProtection/riskDetections and optional riskyUsers (Entra ID P1 or P2). Output is flat for a SIEM, ticketing or a SharePoint list via Power Automate (SharePoint Alert me is being retired). GDAP: Security Reader. Review: user display name added, as in the original register.

title: Sync Office 365 user activity and usage with IT Glue
replaces: AzureAD and AzureRM multi-tenant app added to AdminAgents (DAP), plaintext client secret and IT Glue API key, Graph contracts and beta usage reports
notes: Graph usage reports getOffice365ActiveUserDetail, getMailboxUsageDetail, getOneDriveUsageAccountDetail and four activity reports (CSV) joined by user. IT Glue upsert optional with -Apply, one asset per customer instead of one per user, key from SecretManagement. Yammer and activations reports dropped. GDAP: Reports Reader. Review: restored the original D90 period (now -Period), email, Teams, SharePoint and OneDrive activity counts, and contact email domain matching when no map is given.

title: How to connect to delegated Office 365 tenants using the secure app model
replaces: AzureAD app creation (New-AzureADApplication, New-AzureADApplicationPasswordCredential), AdminAgents pre-consent (Add-AzureADGroupMember, DAP only), PartnerCenter module New-PartnerAccessToken, v1.0 token endpoint with resource= for Azure AD Graph and Microsoft Graph, Connect-MsolService -AdGraphAccessToken, Connect-AzureAD -AadAccessToken, client secret and refresh token in plain text files, basic auth plus MFA IP allow-listing for Exchange
notes: The set-up the article performed is now the MspGdap toolkit itself (New-MspPartnerApp with a certificate, Register-MspPartnerToken into a SecretManagement vault, Grant-MspPartnerAppConsent per GDAP customer, docs/02 to docs/04). This script is the read-only 'can I connect' check that replaces the article's final step: Test-MspGdapAccess (effective GDAP roles), Test-MspPartnerAppConsent (missing scopes, optional -ManifestPath), Graph GET /organization with a tenant ID cross-check, and optional Connect-MspExchangeOnline with Get-OrganizationConfig. All permissions it uses are in partner-app.full.json (DelegatedAdminRelationship.ReadWrite.All, Application.ReadWrite.All, Directory.ReadWrite.All, Exchange.Manage). Partner app read of the customer's service principal and grants needs a customer GDAP role that can read applications (Global Reader recommended).

title: How to detect a breach in Microsoft 365
replaces: Connect-ExchangeOnline with the investigator account, Search-UnifiedAuditLog capped at 5000 records, client IPs sent to free ip-api.com over plain HTTP, protection.office.com references
notes: Works-but-outdated: the audit search is kept, now through Connect-MspExchangeOnline with ReturnLargeSet paging, IP normalisation, an audit-enabled check, and locations from Entra sign-in logs instead of a third-party geolocation call. Article prose should say purview.microsoft.com Audit, auditing on by default, Standard 180 days and Premium 1 year. GDAP: Compliance Administrator or Exchange Administrator, plus Reports Reader for sign-in logs. Review: the raw AuditData JSON is now included, as the original saved the full records.

title: Create Dynamic Distribution List based on email domain
replaces: New-DynamicDistributionGroup with WindowsLiveID -eq '*@domain' (broken quote) -> previews members with Get-Recipient -RecipientPreviewFilter, then creates with filter (RecipientTypeDetails -eq 'UserMailbox') -and (WindowsEmailAddress -like '*@domain') behind -Apply/ShouldProcess
notes: Logic change (WindowsEmailAddress -like) applied as the inventory notes suggested, because OPATH wildcards need -like. An existing group with the same name is reported, not changed. Review: Microsoft's filter reference discourages leading wildcards in Exchange Online filters, so the help tells technicians to check the preview count and fall back to a custom attribute filter.
